inspiration: A zone is a folder of small named tables (jump links, boundary box, terrain NIF list, fixtures, water, city), with one loader per table (src/zone_geometry.cpp lines 130-201). Keep the zone as a data bundle with one table per concern.
Zone exits are data rows: a jump point struct plus a per-zone jump table (include/daoc_client_lib/jump_point.h:12). Zone-to-zone travel without code.

A tree swap map: a real model name maps to a replacement model and bark and leaf textures, with cluster lists for variants (include/daoc_client_lib/tree_replacement_map.h:12-36). Themed trees per zone.
Terrain height is read from a PCX image per zone (src/zone_geometry.cpp:201). Authoring heights from an image makes many zone heightfields quick. Sampling code not read.
Water is a separate geometry layer (dungeon_water.h, river_geometry.h) and not baked into terrain. Keep water as its own layer.
Recipes are plain structs of ingredients and a result (craft_recipes.h:11 and :21) with tests. A data-first crafting table.
Parsers collect warnings instead of failing on one bad row (tree_replacement_map.h:31). Good for data-driven zone loading.

briefs.label: Zone data bundle
briefs.why: A zone that is a folder of plain tables can be authored and swapped without touching code.
briefs.keep: One table per concern; named files; one loader per table
briefs.change: Our own table names and JSON format; add spawn caps and respawn fields to the zone table

briefs.label: Themed tree swap by name
briefs.why: A tree swap map lets one zone look different with the same world layout.
briefs.keep: Real model maps to replacement with bark and leaf sets; cluster variants
briefs.change: Swap by biome tag, not by file name; our own tree shapes

briefs.label: Recipe card
briefs.why: A crafting recipe as a small struct makes the crafting loop data.
briefs.keep: Ingredient list plus result struct; tests for the table
briefs.change: Our own economy and item names; quantities set by our rulings
